For **Amazon Bedrock `InvokeModel`**, `service_tier` is **not part of the Anthropic Messages JSON body**. It is a separate, optional **Bedrock runtime request parameter** (`serviceTier` in the API; `service_tier` in SDKs). The Claude body uses `anthropic_version`, `max_tokens`, and `messages`. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_en/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-api.html))

Example:

```json
// InvokeModel request
{
  "modelId": "your-claude-model-id",
  "serviceTier": "priority",
  "contentType": "application/json",
  "accept": "application/json",
  "body": "{\"anthropic_version\":\"bedrock-2023-05-31\",\"max_tokens\":1024,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello\"}]}"
}
```

Valid tiers are `reserved`, `priority`, `default`, and `flex`; if omitted, Bedrock routes to Standard by default. Check that your chosen model supports the tier. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/service-tiers-inference.html?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_x-social-details_comments-action_comment-text))

So **don’t add `"service_tier"` inside `body`** for `InvokeModel`; set it on the Bedrock request. AWS’s Invoke API reference lists the tier as an optional request field, while its Claude Messages body reference does not list it as a model parameter. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_en/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-api.html))

Citations:

- 1: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_en/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-api.html

- 3: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_en/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-api.html

**Keep `service_tier` out of the Anthropic request body.**

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow retrying canceled jobs from the stopping state**

A summary job normally belongs to a meeting in `stopping` while queued, and `ADMIN_CANCEL_JOB_SQL` changes only the job to `canceled`; it does not change the meeting to `failed`. Consequently, canceling a queued summary job and then calling the retry endpoint always returns 409 at this predicate, leaving the meeting stuck in `stopping`. Accept the state produced by cancellation, or atomically transition the meeting when canceling.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Coordinate the audio check with retention deletion**

When retention cleanup or a manual raw-audio deletion has already selected this failed meeting, it can delete the files after the handler's filesystem probe but before this statement. The cleanup marker remains NULL until its later database phase, so the stale `$4=true` still queues the job and restores the meeting to `stopping` even though both retry inputs are now absent. The row lock does not cover filesystem deletion; retry and retention need a shared reservation/lock or another coordinated validation step.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

To ensure that the DUT configuration is safely cleaned up even if the configuration push fails and aborts the test early, register the cleanup operation using `t.Cleanup()` before executing `configureDUT`.

```suggestion
	t.Cleanup(func() { cleanupDUT(t, env) })
	configureDUT(t, env)
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. All cleanup operations, whether for gNMI configurations or raw CLI commands, must be registered using `t.Cleanup()` to guarantee they are executed even if the test fails or panics early. <sup>([link](https://github.com/openconfig/featureprofiles/blob/main/.gemini/styleguide.md))</sup>
2. Always register cleanup operations using 't.Cleanup()' before executing configuration pushes (e.g., 'b.Set()') or destructive operations (e.g., 'gnmi.Delete()'). This ensures that the cleanup routine is safely queued and will execute to restore the system state even if the operation fails and aborts the test.
</details>

**🟠 High · Linked part metadata goes unchecked**

When multiple backups link to the same stored part but one backup’s checksum, file list, or encryption flag differs, `_objects.setdefault` retains only the first backup’s part metadata, and `_check_part` validates that representative while attributing its result to every linked backup. The other backup’s metadata is unchecked, so it is reported intact when the retained metadata passes.

Validate each linked backup’s part metadata rather than relying on the first representative.

**WARNING:** SQLite parameter limit can cause loan deletion to fail

`deleteTransactionsByIds` uses `WHERE id IN (:ids)` which expands each ID to a bind parameter. SQLite limits bind parameters to 999 (pre-API 26) or 32766 (API 26+). A loan with many linked payments (>999) would cause this query to fail at runtime. Room does not auto-chunk IN clauses.

Consider chunking the ID list in `LoanDelegate.deleteLoan` before calling this DAO method, similar to how `stampPersonIdsOnTransactions` chunks at 900 in `MIGRATION_7_8`.

`pytest_ignore_collect` is a first-result hook. Returning `False` for selected files stops pytest's built-in handler and any other plugin or conftest handlers that run after this one. That built-in handler implements `--ignore`, `--ignore-glob`, and `collect_ignore`/`collect_ignore_glob`. If `tests/run_tests.py` or a conftest relies on any of these, they are silently bypassed for selected files. Files that should be excluded then get collected and run in the batch. Return `True` only for unselected files and `None` otherwise, so the other hooks still run: ```python if collection_path.is_file() and collection_path.suffix in (".py", ".ipynb"): if collection_path.resolve() not in _SELECTED_TEST_PATHS: return True return None ``` ```suggestion def pytest_ignore_collect(collection_path: Path, config: Config) -> bool | None: if collection_path.is_file() and collection_path.suffix in (".py", ".ipynb"): if collection_path.resolve() not in _SELECTED_TEST_PATHS: return True return None ``` *Spotted by [Graphite](https://app.graphite.com/diamond/?org=Genesis-Embodied-AI&ref=ai-review-comment)*
